title: Amos's Words of Judgment Against the Nations and Israel
description: Amos, a shepherd from Tekoa, receives the Lord's message during the reigns of kings Uzziah and Jeroboam. In a series of judgments, he declares the Lord's punishment against Damascus, Gaza, Tyre, Edom, Ammon, Moab, Judah, and finally Israel for their sins, including violence, breaking covenants, and social injustice.

versions.title: Amos's Call and Message
versions.description: Amos, a shepherd from Tekoa, receives God's message about judgment against Israel and the surrounding nations. Through a series of judgments, he exposes their sins, including social injustice and violation of God's law.
versions.reason: [minor] references: Amos' oracles of judgment against the nations continue with Israel as the main target. Chapters 1–2 form a coherent unit with judgments against the seven nations, culminating in judgment against Israel, so the delimitation is reasonable.; [minor] description: The description says 'judgment on Israel and the surrounding nations', but in 1:1–2:16 the judgment is primarily against the surrounding nations (Damascus, Gaza, Tyre, Edom, Ammon, Moab) as well as Judah and Israel. This can be clarified.
